exposure: Retroverted (RV) uterus noted on nuchal translucency (NT) ultrasound
cohort: Patients with a retroverted uterus documented on NT ultrasound at a single academic medical center, from October 2019 to March 2023, compared to anteverted controls, excluding those with multiple gestation, Mullerian anomalies, or fetal aneuploidy.
finding: Persistent retroverted uterus in the first trimester is associated with an increased risk of first-trimester vaginal bleeding, although rates of pregnancy loss were similar between groups.
